questions.question: On a long downhill slope, how should you brake?

options.text: Use only the brakes.
Use mostly brakes and downshift once in a while.
Downshift first, then use the brakes.
Never use the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Downshift first, then use the brakes.
questions.explanation: On a downhill slope, use your engine's braking power to control your speed. Save your brakes for extra slowing or stopping if needed.

questions.question: A 40-foot load on a flatbed trailer must be secured with at least how many tie-downs?

options.text: One tie-down.
Two tie-downs.
Three tie-downs.
Four tie-downs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Four tie-downs.
questions.explanation: On flatbed trailers, use at least one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo. Always use at least two tie-downs, no matter the cargo size.

questions.question: What is the rule about texting while driving?

options.text: It is okay if the messages are short.
It is encouraged.
It is allowed if you are asking your employer a question.
It is not allowed.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is not allowed.
questions.explanation: You cannot send or read text messages while driving.

questions.question: For a vehicle with air brakes, what is the maximum air leakage allowed during an applied leakage test?

options.text: 3 psi in one minute.
6 psi in one minute.
8 psi in one minute.
4 psi in one minute.

questions.correctAnswerText: 3 psi in one minute.
questions.explanation: A vehicle with air brakes should not lose more than 3 psi in one minute during an applied leakage test.

questions.question: When loading a trailer, what is most important about weight distribution?

options.text: Put as little weight as possible over the axles.
Put the right amount of weight over the axles.
Do not worry about how weight is spread out.
Put weight only over the axles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put the right amount of weight over the axles.
questions.explanation: Cargo weight should be balanced evenly in the trailer. Too much or too little weight on an axle makes the vehicle hard to control and can damage the axle.

questions.question: During a vehicle inspection test, which of the following is NOT required about the oil?

options.text: Show where the dipstick is located.
Show the oil level is in a safe range.
Show the oil level is above the refill mark.
Show the oil level is below the refill mark.

questions.correctAnswerText: Show the oil level is below the refill mark.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you must show where the dipstick is, that oil is in a safe range, and that oil is above the refill mark. You should NOT show that oil is below the refill mark.

questions.question: What happens if you pump the brake pedal too much on an air brake system?

options.text: Air leaves the system faster than the compressor can replace it.
More air is added to the brake system.
The brake pedal becomes harder to press.
A loud noise is created.

questions.correctAnswerText: Air leaves the system faster than the compressor can replace it.
questions.explanation: Pumping the brake pedal too much can release air from the system faster than the compressor can refill it. This can lower the air pressure too much and cause brake failure.

questions.question: When do spring brakes activate?

options.text: When air pressure drops too low.
When you press a control on the dashboard.
When tires have worn tread.
When the brakes make noise.

questions.correctAnswerText: When air pressure drops too low.
questions.explanation: Spring brakes turn on automatically when air pressure falls to an unsafe level. Do not wait for this to happen. Exit the road safely and stop the vehicle as soon as you see a low pressure warning.

questions.question: When can mirror adjustment be checked correctly on a tractor with a trailer?

options.text: When the trailer is straight.
When there is no trailer attached.
When the vehicle is on a slight uphill.
When the vehicle is on a slight downhill.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the trailer is straight.
questions.explanation: When a trailer is attached to a tractor, mirrors can only be adjusted correctly if the trailer is straight.

questions.question: How should you do pre-trip inspections?

options.text: Do them the same way each time.
Check different items each time.
Check items in different orders each time.
You do not need to check every item each time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do them the same way each time.
questions.explanation: Always do pre-trip inspections the same way. This helps you remember all the important steps and makes sure you do not skip anything.

questions.question: When you press the brake pedal and the S-cam turns, what does the S-cam do?

options.text: Presses the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum.
Tightens the brake drum onto the axle.
Presses the brake lining against the wheel.
Releases air from the air tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Presses the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum.
questions.explanation: The S-cam presses the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum. This creates friction and slows the vehicle.

questions.question: Exhaust system parts should be:

options.text: Loose.
Leaking.
Fastened securely.
Cracked.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fastened securely.
questions.explanation: Exhaust system parts must be properly fastened. They should not be loose, broken, or missing. Parts should not rub against other parts of the vehicle.

questions.question: Why is it most important to inspect your vehicle before a trip?

options.text: To ensure safety.
To maximize gas mileage.
To wake up before the drive.
To fill up time.

questions.correctAnswerText: To ensure safety.
questions.explanation: Vehicle inspections before every trip are required by state and federal law. They protect you and others on the road.

questions.question: When should you use the parking brake?

options.text: Whenever you park your vehicle.
While driving.
When driving in bad weather.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: Whenever you park your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Use the parking brake every time you park a vehicle with air brakes.

questions.question: What should you use to put out an electrical fire?

options.text: Water.
A B or C extinguisher.
An X extinguisher.
A Q extinguisher.

questions.correctAnswerText: A B or C extinguisher.
questions.explanation: B and C type fire extinguishers work on electrical fires. Never use water on an electrical fire because it can cause electrical shock.

questions.question: How should you use your mirrors while driving?

options.text: Do not use the passenger side mirror.
Do not use the driver's side mirror.
Use both mirrors.
Look in each mirror for long stretches of time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both mirrors.
questions.explanation: To drive safely, know what is happening on all sides of your vehicle. Check both mirrors frequently.

questions.question: Which is NOT a good rule for using turn signals?

options.text: Signal early.
Signal continuously.
Skip your turn signal if you think others know what you plan to do.
Cancel your signal after the turn is completed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Skip your turn signal if you think others know what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: Always signal when you turn or change lanes, no matter what you think others know. Signal early, signal continuously during the turn, and cancel the signal when finished.

questions.question: Which statement about a suspension system is true?

options.text: It has a weight capacity rating.
It uses pressurized water to support the load.
It can handle any weight load.
It has a minimum weight rating.

questions.correctAnswerText: It has a weight capacity rating.
questions.explanation: Suspension systems have weight capacity ratings set by manufacturers.

questions.question: How can you warn drivers behind you that you are about to slow down?

options.text: Slam on the brakes.
Tap the brakes lightly a few times before braking.
Turn on one set of turn signals.
Put your hand out the driver's window and wave.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tap the brakes lightly a few times before braking.
questions.explanation: Lightly tap your brake pedal a few times to flash your brake lights. This warns drivers behind you that you are slowing down.

questions.question: What should you do if you feel drowsy while driving?

options.text: Push on and finish the trip.
Take drugs to stay awake.
Stop and take a nap.
Stop for a coffee break.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and take a nap.
questions.explanation: The only effective way to fight drowsiness is to stop and sleep. Caffeine and other drugs may help temporarily, but they wear off and leave you more tired.

questions.question: When you start a truck with a trailer, how do you know if the Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) is not working?

options.text: The yellow light on the back of the trailer stays on.
The red light on the trailer flashes three times and then stays on.
All the back lights on the trailer flash and then turn off.
The blue light near the driver's door lights up.

questions.correctAnswerText: The yellow light on the back of the trailer stays on.
questions.explanation: Trailers with ABS have a yellow warning light on the left rear. If this light stays on after you start the engine, the ABS is broken.

questions.question: What can happen if you use the parking brake in very wet weather when it is below freezing?

options.text: The brakes will squeak.
The brakes may freeze and the vehicle cannot move.
The brakes may release by themselves.
The brakes may explode.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brakes may freeze and the vehicle cannot move.
questions.explanation: If you use the parking brake in very wet and freezing weather, the brakes can freeze. This stops the vehicle from moving.

questions.question: During a basic vehicle control skills test, you may be asked to:

options.text: Pull forward into a parking space.
Drive in a figure eight.
Back into an alley dock.
Sound your horn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Back into an alley dock.
questions.explanation: The basic vehicle control skills test may include straight line backing, offset back/right parking, offset back/left parking, driver side parallel parking, conventional parallel parking, and alley docking.

questions.question: If your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks, what should you do?

options.text: Stay in the vehicle and try to restart it.
Get out of the vehicle and walk away from the tracks.
Try to flag down another vehicle to push you.
Wait in the vehicle for a police officer to arrive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out of the vehicle and walk away from the tracks.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks, leave the vehicle right away and get away from the tracks. Look for emergency contact information on signs at the crossing. Call that number or call 911.

questions.question: One way to deal with blind spots is to:

options.text: Drive faster than other vehicles so no one can pass you.
Drive in the left lane so you only need to watch vehicles to your right.
Check your mirrors often and watch where other vehicles are.
Do not use your mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors often and watch where other vehicles are.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often to see the traffic around you. This helps you notice if other vehicles are moving into your blind spots.

questions.question: The brake pedal is part of which brake system?

options.text: The service brake system
The parking brake system
The emergency brake system
The auxiliary brake system

questions.correctAnswerText: The service brake system
questions.explanation: The service brake system applies and releases the brakes when the driver presses the brake pedal while driving.

questions.question: What is the best way to check your lights during a pre-trip inspection?

options.text: Park near a mirror and look for a reflection.
Turn on the lights, then get out of the vehicle to check them.
Look at the instrument panel to see if any warning lights are on.
Drive in traffic and wait for other drivers to tell you if lights are out.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on the lights, then get out of the vehicle to check them.
questions.explanation: During a pre-trip inspection, turn on your lights and then get out of the vehicle to look at them.

questions.question: The suspension system:

options.text: Holds up the vehicle and its load.
Keeps the load the right distance behind the driver's area.
Keeps a safe distance between your vehicle and other vehicles.
Makes the load lighter for the tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: Holds up the vehicle and its load.
questions.explanation: The suspension system holds up the vehicle and its load while keeping the axles in place. Damage to the suspension system is very dangerous.

questions.question: What happens if one-fourth of the leaves in a leaf spring are missing during an inspection?

options.text: The driver can drive but only at lower speeds.
The vehicle cannot be driven until it is fixed.
The vehicle is fine to drive since most of the spring is still there.
The driver must carry less weight in the load.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle cannot be driven until it is fixed.
questions.explanation: If at least one-fourth of the leaves in a leaf spring are missing, the vehicle cannot be driven until the problem is fixed.

questions.question: If a CMV driver operates a CMV with a blood alcohol level (BAC) that is lower than 0.04 percent, what happens?

options.text: They will be told to stop drinking.
They will not be allowed to drive for 24 hours.
They must drive at speeds below 55 mph.
They will be told to drive home.

questions.correctAnswerText: They will not be allowed to drive for 24 hours.
questions.explanation: If you operate a CMV with any amount of alcohol in your system below the legal limit of 0.04 percent, you will not be allowed to drive for 24 hours. Operating a motor vehicle while under the influence of alcohol is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: What does the air compressor governor do?

options.text: Controls when the air compressor pumps air into the storage tanks.
Controls how fast air leaves the storage tanks.
Controls the temperature of air going into the storage tanks.
Controls the temperature of air leaving the storage tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Controls when the air compressor pumps air into the storage tanks.
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor controls when the air compressor pumps air into the storage tanks in an air brake system.

questions.question: When going down a steep hill, what should be your main way to slow down?

options.text: Use engine braking by downshifting.
Use the foot brake.
Use the parking brake.
Use ABS.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use engine braking by downshifting.
questions.explanation: On a steep downhill, use the engine's braking power as your main way to control speed. Slow down and downshift before you start going down the hill.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT another name for a convex mirror?

options.text: Fisheye mirror
Spot mirror
Bug-eye mirror
Flat side mirror

questions.correctAnswerText: Flat side mirror
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors are also called fisheye, spot, or bug-eye mirrors. They are not called flat side mirrors.

questions.question: In a truck with air brakes, what does the air compressor do?

options.text: Pumps air into the storage tanks.
Fills the tires.
Moves air to the back of the truck.
Cleans the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pumps air into the storage tanks.
questions.explanation: The air compressor pumps air into the storage tanks. The air compressor governor controls when this happens.

questions.question: What type of air brake system do most heavy-duty vehicles use?

options.text: Mono air brake system
Dual air brake system
Triple air brake system
Quadruple air brake system

questions.correctAnswerText: Dual air brake system
questions.explanation: Most heavy-duty vehicles use dual air brake systems. This system has two separate air brake systems that share one set of controls.

questions.question: If your tractor has ABS but your trailer does not, what will the ABS do?

options.text: It will not work.
It will still help you steer better.
It will make jackknifing more likely.
It will make your brake lights brighter.

questions.correctAnswerText: It will still help you steer better.
questions.explanation: When only the tractor has ABS but the trailer does not, ABS will still improve steering control. Watch your trailer and release the brakes if it starts to swing out.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a distraction while driving?

options.text: Adjusting the radio
Adjusting the CD player
Eating
Checking your mirrors

questions.correctAnswerText: Checking your mirrors
questions.explanation: Anything that takes your attention from driving is a distraction. This includes eating, drinking, smoking, or adjusting the radio or climate controls. Checking mirrors is part of safe driving.

questions.question: Joggers wearing headphones:

options.text: Are usually aware of their surroundings.
May not be aware of their surroundings.
Can clearly hear traffic sounds.
Usually don't have music playing.

questions.correctAnswerText: May not be aware of their surroundings.
questions.explanation: Be careful around pedestrians, joggers, and cyclists wearing headphones. They may not hear traffic clearly and may not know you are there.

questions.question: Why is a vehicle's center of gravity important?

options.text: It usually does not affect how the vehicle handles.
It greatly affects your ability to safely handle the vehicle.
It does not matter when loading cargo.
It only matters if there are hills on your route.

questions.correctAnswerText: It greatly affects your ability to safely handle the vehicle.
questions.explanation: A vehicle's center of gravity is very important for safe handling. Always load cargo as low as possible.

questions.question: During the on-road driving test, which gear action should you avoid?

options.text: Grinding or clashing gears
Selecting a gear that revs the engine too much
Failing to shift through an intersection
Shifting while taking a turn

questions.correctAnswerText: Shifting while taking a turn
questions.explanation: During the on-road driving test, you will be graded on gear use. Choose a gear that does not rev or strain the engine. Avoid grinding gears. Do not shift through turns or intersections.

questions.question: What should you do when carrying a wide load?

options.text: Drive as fast as possible.
Get special permits and follow special rules, like driving only at certain times.
Honk at other drivers to make them move out of your way.
Drive on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get special permits and follow special rules, like driving only at certain times.
questions.explanation: Wide loads need special permits. They can only be driven at certain times and may need special warning signs or equipment.

questions.question: How do you check for a leak in hydraulic brakes?

options.text: Pump the brake pedal three times and hold it for five seconds. If the pedal moves, there may be a problem.
Push the brake pedal all the way down and let go. If it doesn't return to normal position, there may be a problem.
Push the brake pedal all the way down and let go. If the brake squeaks, there may be a problem.
Remove the rear wheel and listen for noise when you press the brake pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pump the brake pedal three times and hold it for five seconds. If the pedal moves, there may be a problem.
questions.explanation: Pump the brake pedal three times, then press it firmly and hold for five seconds. The pedal should not move. If it does, there may be a leak or another problem in the braking system.

questions.question: When should mirrors be adjusted?

options.text: While you are driving.
When the trailer is straight.
When you are standing next to the vehicle.
By someone else.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the trailer is straight.
questions.explanation: Check mirrors before you start driving. On a vehicle with a trailer, you can only adjust mirrors correctly when the trailer is straight.

questions.question: What is the best way to avoid glare from oncoming headlights at night?

options.text: Wear sunglasses.
Close your eyes as the vehicle approaches.
Look toward the right side of the road.
Use your high beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: To avoid being blinded by oncoming lights, look toward the right side of the road until the vehicle passes.

questions.question: What is removed when an air tank is drained?

options.text: Water and oil
Ammonia
Wood
Chlorine

questions.correctAnswerText: Water and oil
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks have drains to remove water and compressor oil. These can damage the brakes if they build up in the system.

questions.question: When might a truck need to stay under the legal maximum weight limit?

options.text: On a flat road.
On a mountainous road.
In heavy traffic.
At night.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a mountainous road.
questions.explanation: In some driving conditions, it is not safe to drive at full legal weight. Be careful in bad weather and on mountainous roads.

questions.question: Why do dry bulk tanks require special care?

options.text: They have low centers of gravity.
They have high centers of gravity.
Loads are usually stable.
They are usually overloaded.

questions.correctAnswerText: They have high centers of gravity.
questions.explanation: Dry bulk tanks have high centers of gravity and their loads often shift during driving. Be especially careful when turning or taking curves.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a cause of vehicle fires?

options.text: Under-inflated tires
Electrical system failures
Flammable cargo
Rolling down the window

questions.correctAnswerText: Rolling down the window
questions.explanation: Vehicle fires can be caused by spilled fuel, under-inflated tires, electrical failures, smoking near fuel, improper refueling, and flammable cargo that is not properly sealed or ventilated. Rolling down a window does not cause fires.

questions.question: How does doubling your speed from 20 mph to 40 mph affect braking distance?

options.text: It stays about the same.
It increases slightly.
It doubles.
It quadruples.

questions.correctAnswerText: It quadruples.
questions.explanation: When you double your speed, braking distance increases by four times. Doubling speed from 20 to 40 mph multiplies braking distance by four.

questions.question: What is the stab braking method?

options.text: Apply full brakes until wheels lock up, release until wheels roll again, then repeat.
Apply brakes halfway while keeping wheels rolling.
Apply full brakes until wheels lock up and the vehicle stops.
Apply the emergency brake until the vehicle starts to slow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply full brakes until wheels lock up, release until wheels roll again, then repeat.
questions.explanation: For emergency stops using stab braking, apply the brakes fully until they lock up. Then release them until the wheels start rolling. Repeat this process.
